subject: Recap + procurement paths: PO vs card vs AWS Marketplace for Polaris
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@polarisinsurance.com>, procurement@polarisinsurance.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + procurement options for Polaris integration

Hi Lena / Procurement team,

Great to speak with you all earlier — thanks for walking through Polaris' use case and expected production timeline. Quick recap and the procurement/commercial paths we discussed so we can pick the smoothest route to getting you live: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Technical: initial pilot will run 3 endpoints (chat gen, embeddings, reranking) with PII controls and VPC peering for telemetry.
- Target go-live: Q3 pilot kickoff, scaling to production after evaluation (goal: mid-Q4).

Commercial/procurement paths (pros/cons):
1) Purchase via card (fastest): immediate access, month-to-month billing, best for proof-of-concept. No PO required but may not meet finance controls.
2) PO / invoice (preferred by many enterprises): Redwood issues invoice, standard Net30/Net45 terms; requires vendor form + W-9 + approved PO number. Good for central procurement but adds lead time.
3) Cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure): Quick procurement via Marketplace subscription and consolidated billing; ideal if you want minimal vendor paperwork. Note: some customers prefer Marketplace for faster internal approvals but it does have a different invoicing flow and sometimes affects refund/credits handling.

Action items for us if Polaris wants to pursue PO route (what we'll provide):
- Fill and return your vendor form (attached).
- Provide a short, redline-friendly MSA + SOW-lite tailored to the pilot.
- Provide an example PO/invoice and a pricing comparison (card vs PO vs AWS Marketplace) so finance can evaluate unit economics.

Attachments I included: Polaris-MAP-draft.pdf (high-level mutual action plan), pricing-sheet.xlsx (3-tier estimates card/PO/marketplace).

Can you confirm: 1) which commercial path procurement prefers (PO vs card vs AWS Marketplace), 2) primary billing contact, and 3) any internal deadline for signing (e.g., quarter-end approvals)? If PO, who should we expect to receive the official vendor form/PO number from and what lead time do you estimate?

Proposed next step: I can send a one-page MSA + SOW-lite for quick legal review by EOD tomorrow if that helps speed things up. Would Marissa be OK to coordinate directly with your legal contact?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync if that speeds decisions.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0199
From: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@polarisinsurance.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, procurement@polarisinsurance.com
Cc: Jonathan Kim <jon.kim@polarisinsurance.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement options for Polaris integration

Thanks Diego — helpful recap. Quick answers from procurement side: 

1) Preferred path: PO / invoice is our standard for third-party vendors for anything that becomes part of our production stack.
2) Billing contact: procurement@polarisinsurance.com (I'm looping Jon who sits in vendor management).
3) Timeline: vendor onboarding typically takes 3-4 weeks once we have a completed vendor form and SOC2/assurance docs. If it's urgent, we can consider Marketplace but we'd need to confirm whether Platform spend needs to flow through our centralized marketplace procurement.

I've attached the Polaris vendor form filled in and returned (vendor_form_received.pdf). Also, our vendor mgmt team needs a short list of security artifacts (SOC 2 report summary, subprocessor list, data handling policy). Can Redwood provide a one-page SOC2 summary and a list of subprocessors?

If you can provide the MSA + SOW-lite and an invoice example, I'll circulate internally and confirm next steps.

-Lena
Lena Brooks
Director, Vendor Procurement | Polaris Insurance
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@polarisinsurance.com>, Jonathan Kim <jon.kim@polarisinsurance.com>, procurement@polarisinsurance.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement options for Polaris integration

Diego / team — looping in legal and sales ops notes to move this along.

Lena: thanks for the vendor form — that's great. For speed, we recommend the following approach: 
- We'll provide a short MSA (standard Redwood template) with a SOW-lite that limits initial scope to the pilot. Ask your legal to review that first; keep redlines minimal to hit your 3-4 week target.
- Payment terms: our default is Net30; we can negotiate Net45 if necessary for enterprise finance — Ben, can you prepare a draft invoice example showing Net30 terms and a Marketplace-equivalent purchase price so procurement can compare?
- Security artifacts: attaching redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (one-pager) and a link to our security portal. If procurement requires full SOC2 report under NDA, we can arrange that via our security team.

Diego — I'll take a first pass on the MSA and SOW-lite today and share with you both. Ben — please add the invoice and sample PO language.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Thanks Lena / Jon — appreciate the quick responses and the completed vendor form. Next steps from Redwood to keep your vendor onboarding moving: 

1) Deliverables by EOD Mon (2027-06-07):
   - Draft MSA + SOW-lite for pilot (Marissa to take lead)
   - Pricing comparison (card vs PO vs AWS Marketplace) and example invoice/PO language (Ben)
   - One-page SOC2 summary + subprocessors list (attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf)
   - Filled vendor form acceptance confirmation (we received vendor_form_received.pdf)

2) Recommendation: If Polaris needs the absolute fastest procurement path for the pilot, AWS Marketplace will usually allow you to subscribe quickly and start testing while we parallel-track the PO. If procurement prefers the MSA/PO route for governance, we'll prioritize MSA + PO paperwork and can target the 3-week window you mentioned. Tradeoff: Marketplace is fastest; PO gives you centralized vendor control and longer-term invoicing flexibility.

3) Proposed timing:
- Mon/Tue: Redwood sends draft MSA + SOW + invoice example.
- Wed: Procurement legal/finance gives initial feedback.
- Following week: Finalize PO and sign (if PO route chosen) — target to have pilot start within 2-3 weeks after PO issuance.

Would you like a 20-minute sync next week (Tue/Wed) to review the MSA and the pricing comparison together with finance/vendor mgmt? I'm available Tue 10-11am or Wed 2-3pm PT.

I'll upload the documents to the HubSpot deal and send DocuSign templates once we have agreement on the path. DocuSign preview link: https://www.docusign.com/templates/rdw-ms-2027-2371
